module_title: Intermediate Matrix - Musical Instruments and their Legendary Maestros
introduction: This level focuses purely on mapping legendary artists to their specific musical instruments and respective Gharanas. UPPSC Prelims features a guaranteed 'Match the Following' question testing your ability to differentiate a Sitar player from a Tabla player.

core_concepts.title: Tabla Players (Primarily Benares Gharana)
core_concepts.description:
- **Kishan Maharaj** (Benares Gharana)
- **Gudai Maharaj** (real name Samta Prasad - Benares Gharana)
- **Anokhelal Mishra** (Benares Gharana)
- **Lachhu Maharaj** (Note: He was both a legendary Kathak dancer of Lucknow and a renowned Tabla player).

core_concepts.title: Sitar Players
core_concepts.description:
- **Pandit Ravi Shankar:** Benares (Awarded the Bharat Ratna, he is India's biggest global music ambassador).
- **Ilyas Khan:** Lucknow Gharana.

core_concepts.title: Kathak Dancers (The Maharaj Dynasty of Lucknow)
core_concepts.description:
- **The 'Maharaj' Family:** If a name ends with 'Maharaj' (with one major exception), they are legendary Kathak dancers belonging to the Lucknow Gharana.
- **Examples:** Birju Maharaj, Shambhu Maharaj, Acchan Maharaj, Bindadin Maharaj.

core_concepts.title: Shehnai & Sarangi
core_concepts.description:
- **Shehnai:** Ustad Bismillah Khan (Benares Gharana - Bharat Ratna 2001).
- **Sarangi:** Pandit Ram Narayan and Shiyaji Mishra (Benares Gharana).

important_entities.name: Girija Devi
important_entities.significance: A legendary vocalist of the **Benares Gharana**, Girija Devi elevated semi-classical genres like Thumri, Chaiti, and Kajri to global prominence. She is universally celebrated as the 'Queen of Thumri'.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
This is the most lethal trap in UP exams:
- **Kathak Dancers (Lucknow):** Birju Maharaj, Shambhu Maharaj.
- **Tabla Player (Benares):** **Kishan Maharaj**. 
Never match Kishan Maharaj with Kathak dance; he was strictly a Tabla maestro.

While Pt. Ravi Shankar was born in Benares and represents its legacy, he actually learned to play the Sitar under Ustad Allauddin Khan of the **Maihar Gharana** (Madhya Pradesh). If the exam asks for his 'training' gharana, look for Maihar.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Pairs the two biggest Benares Tabla names—Kishan Maharaj and Gudai Maharaj (Samta Prasad)—together to avoid mixing them up with Lucknow's dancers.

exam_strategy_tips: Write down the Kathak dancers and Tabla players in two separate columns during your revision. The examiner will almost always try to make you cross-match Birju Maharaj with Kishan Maharaj.
